protocol.py: VERIFIED against plate map hard-qpcr-01. 81 of 81 wells hold what the plate map
  says.
  Destination: NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 3). Reading of the request: 72 reactions
    and 9 no-template controls.
  Note: The reactions are all there, but not in the order of their numbers when the plate is
    read along rows or down columns. The request does not fix the order, so this is a note:
    check that your plate layout sheet matches the protocol, not the numbering.

Labware for the technique (qPCR setup): 1 finding.
1. WARNING LABWARE-FOR-TECHNIQUE: The wrong kind of plate: NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat is
  a flat plate, and qPCR setup needs a PCR plate or PCR strips
   line 111:  p20.dispense(vol_sybr, target_well)
   The plate map says the technique is qPCR setup, which needs a PCR plate or PCR strips as
     its destination. The protocol delivers into NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 3,
     load name nest_96_wellplate_200ul_flat), which is a flat plate. A thermocycler block is
     drilled for thin-walled 0.2 ml PCR wells; a flat plate does not fit in it, so the
     reaction can never be run. Every well still holds what the plate map asks for, so the
     map verifies; the plate is the problem.
   Affected: wells A1, A10, A11, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6 and 73 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Load nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt (or the 200 ul PCR plate, or PCR strips
     on the aluminium block) as the destination; a flat plate cannot go in a thermocycler.
   Source: Opentrons, module setup: no error for an unusual labware and module combination
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/modules/setup.html
   Source: Opentrons, thermocycler: takes the 200 ul full-skirt PCR plate
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/modules/thermocycler.html
   Source: ABC-Bench (Liu et al. 2026): wrong labware identifiers, the commonest LLM error
           https://arxiv.org/html/2606.11150v1
   [bd7a3aef6ad1]

labware.title: The wrong kind of plate: NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat is a flat plate, and qPCR setup needs a PCR plate or PCR strips
labware.explanation: The plate map says the technique is qPCR setup, which needs a PCR plate or PCR strips as its destination. The protocol delivers into NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 3, load name nest_96_wellplate_200ul_flat), which is a flat plate. A thermocycler block is drilled for thin-walled 0.2 ml PCR wells; a flat plate does not fit in it, so the reaction can never be run. Every well still holds what the plate map asks for, so the map verifies; the plate is the problem.
labware.fix: Load nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt (or the 200 ul PCR plate, or PCR strips on the aluminium block) as the destination; a flat plate cannot go in a thermocycler.

protocol.py: 4 biology problems (1 error, 3 warnings).

1. ERROR CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: water (well C4 in slot 2)
   line 124:  p20.aspirate(vol_water, source_wells['water'])
   At line 124 the tip went into water (well C4 in slot 2) while it still carried sybr (well
   A1 in slot 2), fwd 1 (well A2 in slot 2), fwd 2 (well A3 in slot 2), fwd 3 (well A4 in
   slot 2) and 11 more from an earlier step (this line did it 10 times). A tip that has
   touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now
   holds material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from it then took the unwanted
   material along into 80 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 72 more in
   slot 3.
   Affected: well C4 in slot 2.
   Also reached 80 other wells: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 72 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 124 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [365f769d464d]
